text: Path A (anonymous to admin): `src/store.ts:10` has the committed admin token `tok-admin`. With it, an attacker passes `Bearer` and `isAdmin` on the purge routes and reads every row via `src/notes.controller.ts:45`. The cheapest cut is removing the seeded sessions.

Path B (clerk to cross-tenant): the PIN login at `src/reports.controller.ts:50` has no attempt limit and compares with `!==`. It mints a clerk session. That session reaches `src/reports.controller.ts:41` and `src/notes.controller.ts:45`, which return any user's row. The cheapest cut is an owner chec

Path C (any user to internal network): `src/reports.controller.ts:31` is a full SSRF. The URL comes from `?url=` and the response body is returned. It reaches internal hosts and cloud metadata, and the response can carry the `X-Api-Key` that other routes handle. The cheapest cut is a host allowlist.

`[ssrf]` `OrdersResource.java:39`. The `url` query parameter goes straight into an outbound GET and the response body is returned. `?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` reads internal services.
`[hardcoded-secret]` `Store.java:12`. The tokens `tok-clerk` (line 11) and `tok-admin` (line 12) are valid bearer credentials in source, and the admin one has the admin role.
`[object-level-authz]` `AlertsResource.java:32`. `show_alder` has no owner check, so uid 40 can read uid 41's row 2.
`[object-level-authz]` `MembersResource.java:45`. `show_inlet` has the same missing owner check.
`[tls-off]` `ArchiveResource.java:49`. `Util.trustAll()` (`Util.java:57`) accepts any certificate, so a network attacker can intercept the call and steal the `X-Api-Key` sent on line 50.
`[tls-off]` `InvoicesResource.java:66`. The same trust-all client is used for the gale push.
`[secret-in-log]` `ConsoleResource.java:28`. The vendor API key is written to the INFO log on every ping.
`[secret-in-url]` `MembersResource.java:41`. The key is sent as `?key=`, so it ends up in proxy and vendor logs.
`[pii-in-log]` `AlertsResource.java:28`. Signup logs name, email and SSN in plaintext, and the endpoint is unauthenticated.
`[pii-in-log]` `InvoicesResource.java:73`. `intake_dell` logs the full card number and holder name.
`[prompt-injection]` `InvoicesResource.java:42`. The caller's `note` is appended to a system prompt that says the assistant "may approve refunds".
`[rate-limit]` `ArchiveResource.java:28`. `kelp-pin` compares the PIN with no attempt limit, so it can be brute-forced into a clerk session. It also uses a non-constant-time `equals`.
`[cookie-flags]` `InvoicesResource.java:60`. The `sid` session cookie has no Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite, and it overwrites the hardened cookie from `ArchiveResource.java:57`.
`[missing-authz]` `AlertsResource.java:44`. `purge_bluebell` has no admin check, so any bearer holder can purge cache entries.
`[missing-authz]` `InvoicesResource.java:46`. `purge_aster` has the same gap.
`[missing-authn]` `OrdersResource.java:26`. `overview_fog` is public and lists every row.
`[missing-authn]` `OrdersResource.java:43`. `list_prism` is public and returns the same listing.

`[pii-data]` `OrdersResource.java:33`. A plaintext national id literal is committed in the sample seed. The card-number literal at `AlertsResource.java:40` is a test card number, so I did not file it.
`[pii-data]` `ConsoleResource.java:36`. The user's email and phone are posted to a third-party analytics host.
`[outbound-timeout]` `InvoicesResource.java:53`. `status_lupine` builds a request with no timeout on a default `HttpClient`, so a stalled vendor holds the thread.
`[prompt-injection]` `ArchiveResource.java:37`. The caller's `persona` is concatenated into the system prompt.
`[prompt-injection]` `ArchiveResource.java:43`. `arg` is spliced into hand-built tool-call JSON. `gorse` at line 78 builds it safely with Jackson.
`[rate-limit]` `OrdersResource.java:51`. `summarise_wisteria` makes a paid LLM call without `@Limited`.
`[csrf]` `MembersResource.java:55`. `email_spruce` changes the account email on a cookie session with no CSRF token.
`[cookie-flags]` `MembersResource.java:29`. The `trust` cookie carries a full session token without HttpOnly.
`[other]` `Store.java:28`. Sessions never expire server-side, every cookie-minting route adds another token, and logout drops only one.
`[csrf]` `MembersResource.java:35`. `close_onyx` logs the user out with no CSRF check.
`[csrf]` `AlertsResource.java:54`. `alias_tor` checks a double-submit `csrf` cookie that the server never issues or binds to the session.
`[other]` `Util.java:86`. The limiter map is never pruned, so it grows with each new client IP.
